_comment: Canonical service inventory for the ai-stack health checkers — the single
source of truth for WHAT to check, to stop the three checkers from drifting.
Consumed directly by status_check.py (data-driven liveness loop). The
PowerShell monitor (stack-watchdog.ps1) and quick-fixes.bat keep their
bespoke probe/recovery logic but should be reconciled against this list when
containers are added/removed (alongside compose + recovery scripts + stack-map,
per CLAUDE.md's three-place convention).
IMPORTANT: 'container' is the docker container NAME (use with `docker inspect`).
For the ai-stack project some compose SERVICE keys differ from container names
(service redis->search-redis, gateway->search-gateway,
— see the 'service' field where it differs.
Open Brain is a SEPARATE compose project (open-brain); a plain `docker compose`
from the ai-stack dir cannot see it — probe its containers by name.
MACHINE-VERIFIED since 2026-08-22 (D-12): the pre-commit check
(check-project-configs.ps1) diffs every (container -> project) row against
the rendered compose configs - the inventory can no longer drift silently.
Curated fields (critical / host_health / notes) remain hand-owned.
'projects' CARRIES THE COMPOSE INVOCATION (2026-08-28). Each entry has:
file     - compose file, repo-root-relative. null means the project owns
NO services and nothing can be started in it (only 'ai-stack').
env_file - extra --env-file, or null when the project needs none.
compose  - the same thing spelled as a human-runnable command line.
stack-watchdog.ps1 resolves every container repair through this map, so a
plane split cannot leave remediation pointing at a project that no longer
owns the container - which is exactly what Part K did, silently, for 22
self-heal paths between 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-28.

ai-stack.note: PURE NETWORK ANCHOR since Part K.5b (2026-08-21): owns the shared llm-net / app-net / default networks and ZERO services. `docker compose up -d <anything>` here exits 1 with 'no such service'. file=null marks it unstartable; no container row points at it.

open-brain.note: env_file is deliberately null: compose's project directory here is OB1/docker, so it auto-loads OB1/docker/.env. Passing the ROOT .env would override it with the wrong values.

agent-org.note: env_file is deliberately null, same as open-brain: compose's project directory is agent-org/docker, so it auto-loads agent-org/docker/.env. Passing the ROOT .env would override it with the wrong values. The workers/cloud slices are PROFILE-GATED: a bare `config` or `up` renders only the six always-on services, so any tool reading this file must pass --profile workers --profile cloud to see the rest.

core.note: LiteLLM front door (holds the llama-cpp / llama-cpp-embed aliases). No host_health: llm-net is internal so host :4000 is inert; liveliness is in-network (http://llm-gateway:8080/health/liveliness).
B2 admission controller between LiteLLM and the upstreams (llm-backend-net only; liveness via docker exec /healthz)
Admin-UI sidecar (tailnet :8445/ui + litellm.devinveller.ai); serves no inference

search.note: Mullvad egress + kill-switch; ALL search-plane traffic

notebook.note: being retired (Quartz workbench); still live for podcasts
open-notebook DB; WS-only, no HTTP health

openbrain.note: stale-pool dependency: if this restarts after openbrain-mcp, mcp must be restarted
holds a long-lived DB connection that does NOT auto-reconnect; OWUI tool 500s / 'Broken pipe' when stale
MCP->OpenAPI bridge Open WebUI tools call

Ops door (PLAN §1.4): a second openbrain-gateway instance with its own OPS_GATEWAY_KEY, allowlisting the agent_memory_* tools for HOST processes that cannot reach openbrain-mcp (it publishes no host port). Stateless - no backup sidecar. Not critical: without it host callers lose the agent-memory lane; nothing else degrades.
the clock for the whole scheduled chain

backups.note: weekly GGUF-store tar; empty LM_MODELS_BACKUP_INTERVAL disables
Worker journal tarball sidecar (profile-gated with the pool it serves).
Worker journal tarball sidecar (profile-gated with the pool it serves).

agent-org.note: The org's whole operator surface. Its healthcheck uses mmctl, not curl - a curl-based one reported healthy while the server was unusable (see memory: mattermost-mobile-thread-bug).
The governed org bus - orchestrator, gates, workers. Holds a long-lived DB connection; see stale_pool_guard on openbrain-mcp for the same class of failure.
Postgres behind agent-bridge: efforts, gates, constraints, audit.
Worker pool slot 1. Stateless BY DESIGN - the flail guard forks a fresh session; what persists is curated memory, not context.
open-terminal executor for worker 1. GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM=1 lives here.
Git proxy for the worker pool. Hard-denies pushes to main/master (production-branch guard).
Egress proxy for the cloud slice.
Cloud LiteLLM slice; profile-gated and normally down.
Spend ledger for the cloud slice.
